text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Cabinet expected to pass stock exchange law in temporary form this week. Stock exchange chairman says law must be passed quickly to match recently approved companies law. Says importance of law is division between bourse administration and deposit and clearing of shares. Also gives companies the chance to register shares on Arab and international exchanges, and to establish investment funds.

- Government source tells Al-Rai that Jordan has achieved Most Favoured Nation status with the United States on account of its investment accord signed in Washington on Thursday. Says agreement will encourage U.S. investment in Jordan by offering guarantees to potential investors.
- Tourism minister says setting up security force to prevent theft and smuggling of antiquities in Jordan.
- Conference to support Jerusalem opens in Amman today with formal establishment of business group to invest in Jerusalem real estate to protect Palestinian land and property.

- U.S. sources say Secretary of State Madeleine Albright expected to visit Amman, Riyadh, Cairo, Tel Aviv and Gaza for a tour which will go beyond reviving Palestinian-Israeli talks. They say the secret part of King Hussein's talks with President Bill Clinton have paved the way for progress.
- Chance of a meat crisis after Australian Meat and Cattle Organisation pulls out of Free Trade Zone for goats following financial losses.
- King to undergo prostate surgery and meet Israeli premier Netanyahu at Mayo Clinic in United States.
